body.text: You will not know my name and I did not expect to be writing to you. The people who are leaving {param:town} chose me on Tuesday, in the yard, by a show of hands.
We are some ninety miles from anywhere by the time you read this. I shall write again when there is a town to write from.
I am told I should write to you. So: I have written to you.
I am given to understand you may have views about where we settle. I shall be glad of them if they arrive before we stop walking.
I am given to understand you may have views about where we settle. They will find me on the road, or they will not.
I have never governed anything. Neither, I am reliably informed, had the man who governs the place we are leaving.
I have never governed anything, and I would rather you heard that from me than worked it out.

options.text: and wish you a good road
and have views, since you ask
and will be brief, since you are walking

options.label: the best ground he can find
options.text: Settle on the best ground you can find, and do not stop short of it for the sake of your feet.

options.label: toward the coast
options.text: Keep toward the coast. What you make will have to reach a ship.

options.label: near the ore
options.text: Settle near the ore. The colony has hands enough and too little to put in them.

options.label: away from the tribes
options.text: Keep away from the tribes. Whatever the ground is like, I had rather you were left alone on it.

note: Issue 368: founding-towns.md section 5 has the PC's preference arrive in his reply to the governor's first letter; it had no reply. pc.state_a_preference remains for a later word while the party walks.
